record.paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
record.original_question: Let f be a logconcave density on R^n, and let P be any partition of R^n into convex parts. Is there an absolute constant C such that the sum over parts P of σ_f(P)^2 π_f(P) is always at most Cσ_f^2, where σ_f^2 is the largest variance of f in any direction and σ_f(P)^2 is the largest directional variance of the restriction of f to the part P?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 26. Let f be a logconcave density function and P be any partition of R^n such that each part is convex. Then there exists a constant C such that Σ_P σ_f(P)^2 π_f(P) ≤ Cσ_f^2 where σ_f^2 is the largest variance of f along any direction and σ_f(P)^2 is the largest variance of f restricted to the set P.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\mathbb{R}^n	o[0,\infty)$ be a logconcave probability density (i.e. $\log f$ is concave and $\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} f=1$). For any measurable set $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ with $\pi_f(S):=\int_S f>0$, let $f|_S$ denote the restriction (and renormalization) of $f$ to $S$, and define
$$\sigma_f(S)^2 \;=\; \sup_{u\in\mathbb{R}^n,\;\|u\|=1}\; \mathrm{Var}_{X\sim f|_S}\! igl(\langle u,Xangle igr),$$
the largest variance of $f|_S$ along any unit direction. Write $\sigma_f^2:=\sigma_f(\mathbb{R}^n)^2$ for the largest directional variance of $f$ itself.

Prove or disprove: there exists an absolute constant $C>0$ (independent of $n$, $f$, and the partition) such that for every dimension $n\ge 1$, every logconcave density $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, and every partition $\mathcal{P}=\{P_1,P_2,\dots\}$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ into convex measurable parts,
$$\sum_{P\in\mathcal{P}} \sigma_f(P)^2\,\pi_f(P)\;\le\; C\,\sigma_f^2.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is closely related to the Kannan-Lovász-Simonovits (KLS) program and to localization arguments via partitions into convex parts (and ultimately into one-dimensional needles). Although the KLS hyperplane/Cheeger conjecture has seen major progress (Eldan, Lee-Vempala, Chen, Klartag-Lehec) culminating in near-optimal bounds, no source found explicitly resolves this particular partition-variance inequality with a dimension-free constant. Its current status appears unknown from available public literature.

status_evidence.title: The Kannan-Lovász-Simonovits Conjecture (Lee-Vempala survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of KLS conjecture and localization methods partitioning into one-dimensional logconcave needles.
status_evidence.claim: Localization-style partition inequalities are central to KLS but the specific variance-sum conjecture is not reported as resolved.

status_evidence.title: Eldan's stochastic localization and the KLS conjecture (Annals of Math 2024)
status_evidence.claim: Major progress on KLS via stochastic localization, but does not establish the stated partition-variance inequality.
status_evidence.snippet: Improved isoperimetric and concentration bounds for isotropic logconcave measures.
